Definition: from (the alternate of) G3784; something owed, i.e. (figuratively) a due; morally, a fault:--debt.
BiblicalUsage: This is the debt itself, the thing owed. In the prayer Jesus taught, we ask the Father to forgive us our debts as we forgive our debtors, and Paul says that to the one who works, the reward is reckoned not as grace but as debt.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word draws the line between wages and grace: what is owed to me I can demand, but what God gives me is gift, never debt.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
